title.narrative: UN Joint Programme to Strengthen Urban and Rural Resilience and the Conditions for Recovery in Syria (UNJP 2.0)

description.narrative: The UN Joint Programme 2.0 (UNJP 2.0) is a three-year initiative in Syria that brings together six UN agencies (FAO, UNDP, UNFPA, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, and WFP) under the coordination of the UN Resident Coordinator Office (UNRCO) and the leadership of the UN Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator (UNRC/HC). The program is a continuation of efforts started under the Joint Programme Urban Rural Resilience1.0 (2019-2023) and is focused on enhancing the resilience of both rural and urban communities in Syria, particularly in the Aleppo Governorate. The protracted Syrian crisis has resulted in economic collapse, mass displacement, destruction of infrastructure and deeply strained social services, all of which have worsened with recent events, including the 2023 earthquake. UNJP 2.0 seeks to address these challenges through an integrated, area-based, multi-sectoral approach designed to provide sustainable, resilience-building solutions. UNJP 2.0 takes a "Nexus" approach, which aligns humanitarian aid with longer-term early recovery interventions reducing dependency on short-term assistance. The program uses an area-based approach that is flexible, and a community-led approach, ensuring that local stakeholders play a key role in decision-making. This model encourages bottom-up planning, with interventions tailored to the specific needs of the communities of targeted areas. It also promotes interagency collaboration, leveraging the combined expertise of the participating UN agencies. To support this, a pooled funding mechanism administered by the UN Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) enables coordinated efforts that maximize the impact of interventions. Accordingly, the main expected accomplishments of UNJP 2.0 involve: • Strengthening the resilience of communities in Syria, particularly in Aleppo, through integrated, multi-sectoral interventions in areas such as health, education, agriculture, and infrastructure. • Enhancing social cohesion by addressing the root causes of community tensions, including disparities in access to services and livelihood opportunities. • Promoting a community-led, participatory approach to recovery and development, empowering local stakeholders to define and prioritize interventions. • Fostering interagency collaboration and building on the lessons learned from UNJP1.0, aiming for more sustainable, long-term solutions to Syria’s ongoing crises. • Reducing dependence on humanitarian assistance over time by creating more durable and self-sustaining support systems that address immediate needs and long-term recovery efforts. Through these efforts, UNJP 2.0 aims to contribute to the broader goal of moving Syria beyond the cycle of crisis and humanitarian aid dependency toward a more resilient and self-reliant future.
